headline: A miserable Tuesday as the C's and Bruins both drop games
morning_brew: Tuesday was an absolute nightmare for our teams on the road. The C's opened their campaign in Detroit and managed to choke away a twenty-two point lead against the Pistons, which is about the worst way to kick off a season I've ever seen. It was one of those performances that makes you wonder if the team was daydreaming about their vacation plans in the second half. Watching a lead that massive evaporate in the season opener is just brutal for the blood pressure, and I might need to switch to decaf if they keep playing like that.

Over on the ice, the Bruins saw their five-game winning streak snapped in Dallas, and it was a total heartbreaker in overtime. Despite a real gritty effort from Matthew Poitras and James Hagens, the Stars found a way to swipe the extra point. The game was tighter than a pair of jeans after a Thanksgiving dinner, but losing in OT feels like a kick in the shins when you consider how well the boys have been skating. My neighbor Rick is already deep into his conspiracy theory that the refs were wearing Dallas jerseys, and frankly, I am too exhausted to even argue with him this morning.

We have to flush these results and get our heads back in the game. The Bruins return to the Garden on Thursday to handle the Predators, and the C's have a few days to get their act together before the home opener against the Knicks on Friday. It is early, and while nobody enjoys watching a double-header of losses like this, there is plenty of time for both squads to find their rhythm. I am just praying the boys in black and gold can defend our own ice when the Predators hit town.

news_digest.headline: Pistons kick off season vs. Celtics with NBA's largest opening day comeback
news_digest.dans_take: To hold the record for the biggest collapse on opening day is a dubious honor I could have lived without.

news_digest.headline: Mikko Rantanen's overtime hat trick gives the Stars a 3-2 win over the Bruins
news_digest.dans_take: Giving up a hat trick to lose in overtime is a special kind of misery.
